content: Create only dedicated PostgreSQL 18 primary, standby, physical-backup, restored, WAL-archive, socket, log, and artifact paths under one disposable profile root.
Apply Vermory migrations to the primary and provision a replication role plus a non-owner RLS runtime role using synthetic identities.
Seed active fact A, active token A metadata, and one revoked token control before physical backup.
Create a native physical point-in-time base backup and a streaming standby from the dedicated primary.
Commit fact B and authenticated operation i03-pre-failover, then capture the T2 authority fingerprint and target WAL position after standby replay catches up.
Delete fact B, revoke token A, commit later fact C, issue the post-target failover token, and archive the required WAL without changing the frozen T2 target.
Stop the dedicated primary in immediate mode and submit operation i03-transition-failure through the already-created Vermory handler.
Require the transition request to return no successful receipt and persist zero rows.
Promote the streaming standby and wait until it is read-write and no longer in recovery.
Reuse the same runtime store, authentication pool, and handler to persist operation i03-post-promotion without process restart.
Verify pre-failover and post-promotion operations exactly once, transition operation zero times, token controls, RLS policies, and cross-tenant isolation on the promoted primary.
Restore a fresh dedicated cluster from the physical base backup and archived WAL using the exact T2 recovery target position.
Require restored authority to match the T2 fingerprint with facts A and B plus active token A, while excluding the later deletion, revocation, and fact C.
Keep the historical restore quarantined, reset disposable projections, and rebuild them only from restored active authority.
Revoke the historically restored token A, verify its raw value is rejected, issue a new token, and verify authenticated access before service acceptance.

Record versions, WAL positions, fingerprints, counts, durations, failures, quarantine status, projection rebuild, credential re-governance, and explicit same-host non-claims without credentials or process logs.
